text: Your battery percentage is a guess.
Here's how your phone makes it.
There's no way to see inside a battery, so a tiny chip, called a fuel gauge, watches it instead.
First, it counts every bit of charge flowing in and out.
But tiny counting errors pile up over time.
So it also checks the voltage.
The catch? Through the middle of the charge, the voltage barely moves.
So the chip blends both, using a model of your battery: its temperature, its age, and how hard you're pushing it.
When reality disagrees, it corrects the guess.
That's how fifteen percent can turn into three in a minute, or a cold phone can die at thirty.
And zero isn't empty. It's where your phone stops, to protect the battery.
So that number isn't a measurement. It's a very good guess.
Send this to the friend who lives at one percent.
